          type: string
          minLength: 1

        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        postcode:
          title: Postcode
          description: >-
            The 4-digit postcode of the pet owner. Optional; when present it must

            Brisbane -> QLD 4000-4099). A city with no known region accepts any

            otherwise the country code '+61' is assumed and a single leading '0' is
            dropped from the national digits; spaces, dashes and brackets are
            stripped. The result must carry 8 to 15 digits after the '+'. The stored
            and returned value is this E.164 string, e.g. '0412 345 678' becomes
            '+61412345678'.

            when present it is used to derive the read-only 'ageBand'.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '1990-01-01'

          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            Write-only flag used only on create. When true, the owner may be
            created even if another owner already has the same last name and the
            same address (i.e. they share a household). It is never stored or
            returned.

      title: Owner

      allOf:

        - type: object
          properties:

              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name

              title: Initials
              description: >-

              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: >-
                The owner's customer code formatted '<REGION>-<HASH8>', where
                REGION is the region code derived from the postcode (falling back
                to the city) and HASH8 is the first 8 upper-case hex characters of
                SHA-256 over the normalized telephone followed by lastName.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW-1A2B3C4D'
              readOnly: true
            checkDigit:
              title: Check digit
              description: >-
                A single Luhn check digit (0-9) computed over the digits
                contained in the customerCode.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              maximum: 9
              example: 4
              readOnly: true
            householdId:
              title: Household ID
              description: >-
                A stable shared identifier for owners who share a household - the
                same last name at the same address. Assigned when an owner is
                created with 'sharesHousehold' set to true; owners in the same
                household receive the same value. Absent otherwise.
              type: string
              example: '8F14E45FCEEA167A'
              readOnly: true
            identityKey:
              title: Identity key
              description: >-
                The owner's derived identity key, formatted
                '<normalizedTelephone>|<email>|<householdId>' (the email and
                householdId segments are empty when absent). Two owners are
                duplicates exactly when their whole identity keys are equal; a
                create request whose identity key matches an existing owner's is
                rejected with 409.
              type: string
              example: '+61412345678|owner@example.test|8F14E45FCEEA167A'
              readOnly: true
            namesakeCount:
              title: Namesake count
              description: >-
                The number of existing owners that, at the moment this owner was
                created, already shared the same first name and last name
                (compared case-insensitively). Zero when the name was unique on
                create.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            membershipNumber:
              title: Membership number
              description: >-
                The owner's membership number formatted '<customerCode>-M<YY>',
                where YY is the last two digits of the registrationDate year
                (e.g. 'NSW-1A2B3C4D-M26').
              type: string
              example: 'NSW-1A2B3C4D-M26'
              readOnly: true
            membershipLevel:
              title: Membership level
              description: >-
                The owner's numeric membership level, derived on creation.
                Starts at 1, plus 1 when an email is present, plus 1 when the
                owner's namesakeCount is 0, capped at 3. Level 4 is reserved
                for tenure.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 1
              maximum: 3
              example: 3
              readOnly: true
            locality:
              title: Locality
              description: >-

                customerCode (the region code baked into the '<REGION>-<HASH8>'

              type: string
              example: 'NSW'
              readOnly: true

                reached.
              type: boolean

              readOnly: true

              enum:

              readOnly: true

              enum:
                - MINOR
                - ADULT
                - SENIOR
              example: 'ADULT'
              readOnly: true
            pets:
              title: Pets
              description: The pets owned by this individual including any booked vet visits.
              type: array
              items:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'
              readOnly: true
          required:

## Summary

I implemented the soft-match "possible duplicate" rule on the owner create endpoint. When a new owner is not a hard duplicate but shares an existing owner's `lastName` and `postcode` while carrying a **different** telephone, it is still created and flagged.

Changes:

- **`openapi.yml`** — added two read-only fields to the Owner schema: `possibleDuplicate` (boolean) and `possibleDuplicateOf` (int32). The `OwnerDto` is regenerated from this at build time.
- **`Owner.java`** — added a persisted `possibleDuplicateOf` column (Integer) with getter/setter, alongside the existing derived-on-create fields (`customerCode`, `householdId`, `namesakeCount`).
- **Schema files** (hsqldb, h2, mysql, postgres) — added the nullable `possible_duplicate_of` column to the `owners` table.
- **`OwnerMapper.java`** — ignored the two new targets so they're populated in the controller (matching the existing `bulkSignupWarning`/`identityKey` pattern).
- **`OwnerRestControllerV1.java`** — added `possibleDuplicateOf(Owner)`, which runs *after* the hard-duplicate check has passed and returns the id of the first existing owner sharing last name (case-insensitive) and postcode with a different canonical telephone, or `null`. The value is stored on the owner at create time, and `toOwnerDtoWithDerivedFields` sets `possibleDuplicate = (id != null)` and `possibleDuplicateOf = id` on both the create and read responses.

Because the match is captured at creation and persisted, `GET /api/owners/{id}` returns the stable `possibleDuplicateOf` pointing to the pre-existing owner (not a symmetric read-time recomputation) — matching the spec's "shares an existing owner's" semantics.
